draft.title: An interdependent economy
card: An economy has four main groups: consumers, businesses, the financial sector (such as banks) and government. Each one relies on the others.
Consumers earn income by working for businesses and spend it on what businesses sell. Businesses need that spending to pay wages and stay open.
Businesses borrow from banks to grow, and banks rely on being repaid. Government collects taxes from consumers and businesses and spends them on services such as roads and schools.
Because the groups are linked, a decision by one can affect the others. For example, if banks raise loan interest rates, businesses and households may borrow and spend less.
draft.remember: Each group in the economy relies on the others, so one group's decision can affect all of them.

a.q: Why does a decision by one group in an economy often affect the others?
opts: The groups rely on each other for income, funds and services
The groups all make the same decisions at the same time
Government controls what every other group does
The groups only deal with others of the same type
a.why: Consumers, businesses, banks and government depend on each other, so a change by one passes on to the rest. Government collects taxes and provides services, but it does not control every decision made by the others.
a.clue: Think about who pays wages, who lends money and who spends.

b.q: Banks in Perth raise the interest rate on business loans. What is the most likely effect on the other groups?
opts: Businesses borrow less, so they may hire fewer workers
Consumers earn more, because businesses pay higher wages
Government must cut taxes, so that businesses can borrow
Businesses borrow more, so banks have less money to lend
b.why: Dearer loans make businesses borrow and expand less, which can mean fewer jobs and less income for households. Higher wages do not follow from dearer loans, and nothing forces government to cut taxes.
b.clue: Follow the change from the bank to the businesses and then to workers.

a.best: The groups rely on each other for income, funds and services

b.best: Businesses borrow less, so they may hire fewer workers

proposal.remember: Each group in the economy relies on the others, so one group's decision can affect all of them.

a.q: Why does a decision by one group in an economy often affect the others?
opts: The groups rely on each other for income, funds and services
The groups usually make the same decisions at the same time
Government sets the decisions that the other groups make
Each group mostly trades with others of its own type
a.why: Consumers, businesses, banks and government depend on each other for income, loans, spending and services, so a change by one can pass on to the rest. Government collects taxes and provides services, but it does not make the decisions for the other groups.
a.clue: Think about who pays wages, who lends money and who spends.

b.q: Banks in Perth raise the interest rate on business loans. What is the most likely effect on the other groups?
opts: Businesses borrow less, so they may hire fewer workers
Businesses borrow more, so they may hire more workers
Businesses borrow less, so they may pay workers more
Businesses borrow the same, so workers may see no change
b.why: A higher interest rate makes loans dearer, so businesses may borrow and spend less, which can mean fewer jobs and less household income. Borrowing more gets the direction backwards, because dearer loans discourage borrowing rather than encourage it.
b.clue: Does a dearer loan make a business want to borrow more or less?
